en: Harun ibn Ma'ruf and Muhammad ibn Abbad narrated to us—and their wordings of the hadith were close to each other, with the phrasing being that of Harun—both saying: Hatim ibn Ismail narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Mujahid Abu Hazrah, from Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I set out with my father seeking knowledge in this clan of the Ansar before they passed away. The first person we met was Abu al-Yasar, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). With him was a young servant boy of his carrying a bundle of scrolls. Abu al-Yasar was wearing a burdah (striped mantle) and a Ma'afiri cloak, and his servant was also wearing a burdah and a Ma'afiri cloak. My father said to him: 'O uncle, I see on your face the flush of anger.' He said: 'Yes. I was owed wealth by so-and-so, the son of so-and-so, of the Banu Haram. I came to his household, offered greetings of peace, and said: Is he there? They said: No. Then a young son of his who had reached the age of puberty came out to me, so I said to him: Where is your father? He said: He heard your voice and concealed himself behind my mother’s couch. So I said: Come out to me, for I know where you are! He came out, and I said: What made you hide from me? He said: By Allah, I will speak to you and will not lie to you: By Allah, I feared that I would speak to you and lie to you, and promise you and break my promise to you; you are a companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and by Allah, I was in straitened circumstances. He said: I said: By Allah? He said: By Allah. I said: By Allah? He said: By Allah. I said: By Allah? He said: By Allah. He said: Then he brought his written debt document and erased it with his hand, and said: If you find means to repay, repay me; otherwise, you are completely absolved. For I testify that these two eyes of mine saw—and he placed his two fingers upon his eyes—and these two ears of mine heard, and this heart of mine retained—and he pointed to the core of his heart—the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: "Whoever grants respite to a debtor in difficulty or remits debt for him, Allah will shade him in His shade." He said: Then I said to him: 'O uncle, if only you took your servant boy's burdah and gave him your Ma'afiri cloak, and took his Ma'afiri cloak and gave him your burdah, you would have a matching two-piece suit and he would have a matching two-piece suit.' He wiped my head and said: 'O Allah, bless him! O son of my brother, these two eyes of mine saw, these two ears of mine heard, and this heart of mine retained—and he pointed to the core of his heart—the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: "Feed them from what you eat and clothe them with what you wear." And that I should give him from the goods of this worldly life is easier upon me than that he should take from my good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.' Then we proceeded until we came upon Jabir ibn Abdullah in his mosque while he was praying wrapped in a single garment. I walked past the people until I sat between him and the qiblah, and I said: 'May Allah have mercy on you! Do you pray in a single garment while your cloak is lying at your side?' He said: He gestured with his hand toward my chest like this—spreading his fingers and arching them—and said: 'I intended that a fool like you should come in upon me and see how I act, and then do the like of it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came to us in this mosque of ours holding in his hand a branch from the Ibn Tab date palm. He saw phlegm in the qiblah of the mosque and scraped it off with the date-palm branch. Then he turned to us and said: "Which of you would like that Allah should turn away from him?" He said: We became filled with reverent awe. Then he said: "Which of you would like that Allah should turn away from him?" He said: We became filled with reverent awe. Then he said: "Which of you would like that Allah should turn away from him?" We said: None of us, O Messenger of Allah! He said: "When one of you stands to pray, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is before his face, so let him not spit toward his front nor toward his right, but let him spit toward his left under his left foot. If an urge to spit overtakes him suddenly, let him do with his garment like this." Then he folded part of his garment over another part. Then he said: "Bring me perfume." A young man from the clan stood up and hurried to his family, returning with khalūq perfume in the palm of his hand. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took it, placed it on the tip of the date-palm branch, and smeared it over the trace of the phlegm.' Jabir said: 'It was from that incident that you began applying khalūq perfume in your mosques.' We marched with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) on the military expedition of Batn Buwat while he was seeking al-Majdi ibn Amr al-Juhani. Five, six, or seven of us would take turns riding a single water-carrying camel. The turn to ride of a man from the Ansar came upon a camel of his; he made it kneel, mounted it, and then urged it to stand, but it hesitated somewhat. So he said to it: 'Get on! May Allah curse you!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Who is this who curses his camel?" He said: 'It is I, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: "Dismount from it! Do not accompany us with a cursed beast. Do not pray against yourselves, do not pray against your children, and do not pray against your properties, lest you coincide with an hour from Allah wherein a request for a grant is asked and He answers your prayer." We marched with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) until, when evening arrived and we drew near to a water source belonging to the Arabs, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Who is the man that will go ahead of us, plaster the water basin with clay, drink, and provide water for us?" Jabir said: I stood up and said: 'Here is that man, O Messenger of Allah!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Which man will go with Jabir?" Thereupon Jabbar ibn Sakhr stood up. We set out to the well and drew a bucketful or two into the basin, plastered it with clay, and then drew water into it until we filled it to the brim. The first person to arrive upon us was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), who said: "Do you two give permission?" We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He brought his riding camel to the water and it drank; he pulled its halter upward so its neck stretched back, and it urinated. Then he turned it aside and made it kneel. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came to the basin and performed ablution from it. Then I stood up and performed ablution from the ablution-water of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). Jabbar ibn Sakhr went away to relieve himself. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) then stood to pray. I had a burdah on me; I tried to wrap its two ends across each other, but it was not wide enough for me. It had tassels, so I inverted it, crossed its two ends over, gripped it with my neck and shoulders, and then came and stood on the left side of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). He took me by the hand, turned me around, and made me stand on his right. Then Jabbar ibn Sakhr arrived, performed ablution, came and stood on the left side of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took both of our hands together and pushed us until he positioned us behind him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began looking at me closely while I did not realize it; then I noticed him, and he gestured with his hand like this—meaning: fasten your waist tight! When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) finished the prayer, he said: "O Jabir!" I said: 'At your service, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: "When the garment is spacious, cross its two opposite ends; but when it is narrow, wrap and tie it tightly around your waist." We marched with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and the daily sustenance of each man among us was a single date. A man would suck on it and then tie it up in his garment. We would beat leaves off trees with our bows and eat them until the corners of our mouths became ulcerated. I swear that one day a man among us was accidentally passed over and missed his date, so we took him along, supporting him under his arms, and testified that he had not been given it; so it was given to him, and he stood up and took it. We marched with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) until we encamped in a wide, spacious valley. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) went to relieve himself, and I followed him carrying a leather water-skin. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) looked around and saw nothing with which he could screen himself. Behold, there were two trees at the edge of the valley. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) walked over to one of them, took hold of one of its branches, and said: "Yield to me by the permission of Allah!" It yielded along with him like a camel with a wooden nose-ring that readily follows its leader, until he reached the other tree. He took hold of one of its branches and said: "Yield to me by the permission of Allah!" It likewise yielded along with him until, when he was at the midpoint between them, he brought them together—meaning he joined them—and said: "Join together over me by the permission of Allah!" And the two trees joined together. Jabir said: I ran away quickly out of fear that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) might sense my proximity and move further away—and Muhammad ibn Abbad said: 'move further away.' I sat down talking to myself. Then I glanced around, and behold, I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) coming forward, and behold, the two trees had separated and each of them was standing upright upon its own trunk. I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) pause for a moment, gesturing with his head like this—and Abu Ismail gestured with his head right and left—and then he came forward. When he reached me, he said: "O Jabir, did you see my standing place?" I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: "Go to the two trees, cut a branch from each one of them, and bring them with you until, when you stand at my place, let fall one branch on your right and one branch on your left." Jabir said: I stood up, took a rock, broke it, struck off its edge so that it became sharp for me, and then went to the two trees. I cut a branch from each one of them and came dragging them until I stood at the place of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). I placed one branch on my right and one branch on my left. Then I caught up with him and said: 'I have done it, O Messenger of Allah! What was the purpose of that?' He said: "I passed by two graves being punished, so I desired that through my intercession their punishment might be lightened for them as long as the two branches remain moist." He said: We then returned to the camp. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "O Jabir, call for water for ablution." I called out: 'Is there any water for ablution? Is there any water for ablution? Is there any water for ablution?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I could not find a single drop among the riding party.' There was a man from the Ansar who used to cool water for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) in leather water-skins hung on a wooden tripod frame made of palm branches. He said: He said to me: "Go to so-and-so, son of so-and-so, al-Ansari, and see if there is anything in his water-skins." He said: I went to him and examined them, but I found nothing in them except a single drop in the lower spout of one of the water-skins; if I were to pour it out, the dry leather of the vessel would absorb it. So I came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I found nothing in them except a single drop in the lower spout of one water-skin, such that if I were to pour it out, its dry leather would absorb it.' He said: "Go and bring it to me." I brought it to him. He took it in his hand, began speaking words that I did not know what they were, and squeezed it with his hands. Then he gave it to me and said: "O Jabir, call for a large wooden bowl." I called out: 'O large bowl of the riders!' It was brought, carried along, and placed before him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) placed his hand in the bowl like this—spreading his hand and separating his fingers—and placed it at the bottom of the bowl, and said: "Take, O Jabir, pour upon me and say: In the name of Allah." So I poured upon him and said: 'In the name of Allah.' I saw water gushing forth from between the fingers of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). Then the bowl welled up and swirled until it became full. He said: "O Jabir, call whoever has need of water." He said: The people came and drew water until all were fully satisfied. He said: I said: 'Has anyone remained who has a need?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) lifted his hand from the bowl, and it was still brimful. The people complained of hunger to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and he said: "May Allah feed you." We then came to the seashore. The sea surged with a mighty surge and cast ashore a giant sea creature. We kindled a fire at its side, cooked from it, roasted its meat, and ate until we were full. Jabir said: I, and so-and-so, and so-and-so entered—until he counted five people—inside its eye socket, and no one could see us until we came out! We took one of its ribs and arched it, and then summoned the tallest man in the riding party, the largest camel in the riding party, and the highest camel saddle in the riding party, and he passed under it without even bowing his head.
